warm: warms both hands on the mug
smooths the hearth rug with a boot
sets an extra cup without asking
dry: does not look up from the reel
plain: checks the edge of the hex
bright: turns a coin of light over
leans in as if sharing a secret
writes in the margin and smiles

needs.ask: A moss sprig from a hex would settle the kettle.
One creek trout, if the lake is willing.
A violet eel, only if the water is already glowing.
A boar tusk. Blunt is fine. I am not decorating.
A lantern wick. The short one burns too fast.
Anything dry from under the trees. The rain found the lintel.
A rain petal, if the puddles brought one up.
A dusk fish. Fog like this, they rise.
Something that holds in a wind. A wrap, a tusk, a pin.
A wick or a bun for the pop-up. Whichever you pass first.

clear: Nothing in the sky but light.
rain: The rain is soft and not done.
fog: The fog sits on the reeds.
You can hear the path better than see it.
wind: The wind wants every loose hat.
Even the awnings are thinking about it.

timeLines.dusk: Dusk makes it easier, if you can wait.

dry: No rush. Fish keep their own hours.
plain: One thing. Then the board can rest.
bright: I left a margin for whatever you find.
